text.p: Casinos Austria International Ltd (CAIL) said on Thursday that shareholders had approved the A$18 million capital injection from its parent Casinos Austria International Holding GmbH.
The Australian listed casino operator said a placement of 25.7 million shares at 70 cents each would be made to the parent company on December 27.
CAIL said its issued capital will rise to 176 million shares from 150.3 million, with Casino Austria's shareholding raised to 61.5 percent from 54.9 percent.

CAIL chief executive Alex Tucek said in a statement the capital raising would be used to better position the company's financial position in the short and long-term, and allow it to extend its existing casino operations and pursue future development opportunities.
Chairman Ben Macdonald said in a separate statement the groups has seen a significant turnaround in the operational performance.

"The operating performance in the second half of this year shows an improvement over the first half. For 1997, your directors are forecasting that operations will return to profitability," Macdonald told shareholders.
CAIL shares closed 1.5 cents lower at 32 cents.
